title: PEAD Revived: Elastic Net on 12-Quarter SUE History as H174 Pre-Filter
description: Implement a PEAD enhancement layer on top of H174 (confirmed, OOS WR=81.8%, n=22) using Kaczmarek & Zaremba (2025) findings: elastic net regression on the last 12 quarters of standardized unexpected earnings (SUE) history predicts future returns significantly better than using only the most recent EPS surprise. The H174 entry filter already requires EPS surprise >= 0.02; this upgrade replaces the raw EPS surprise signal with the elastic-net-predicted return score trained on full SUE history. Mechanism: the latest earnings surprise is quickly priced in by the market (especially for large-cap stocks in our universe); however, the PATTERN of earnings surprises across 12 quarters (streaks, reversals, acceleration, magnitude trends) contains information that remains overlooked. The elastic net selects and shrinks the most predictive quarterly SUE features while setting irrelevant lags to zero. Implementation: (1) For each event, pull prior 12-quarter EPS history from FMP/yfinance; (2) Train elastic net on IS (2019-2022) with target = 20-trading-day post-earnings return; (3) OOS (2023-present): score each candidate using IS-trained model; replace surprise >= 0.02 gate with ML_score >= IS_median_threshold. Maintain: FinBERT score >= 0.18 gate from H174. Gate: OOS WR > 81.8% (H174 baseline) AND n >= 15. IS: 2019-2022, OOS: 2023-present. Script: backtesting/daily/run_h388_pead_ml_sue.py. Data: yfinance earnings history (quarterly EPS actuals vs estimates).
rationale: Kaczmarek & Zaremba (Finance Research Letters, 2025, DOI:10.1016/j.frl.2025.108751) find that elastic net on 12-quarter SUE history nearly doubles Sharpe ratios vs single-quarter SUE. Gains are especially strong for large-cap stocks — exactly our H174 universe. The 12-quarter look-back means structural earnings patterns (momentum, reversal, cyclicality) are captured without overfitting to a single quarter. H174's weakness is that EPS surprise >= 0.02 is a blunt threshold — it doesn't distinguish between a company that has beaten 11 of 12 quarters vs one making its first beat. This ML score is a direct upgrade to the most operationally active PEAD filter we run in paper trading daily.
